newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten denounces post-1997 legislature.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten denounces post-1997 legislature.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten on Saturday sharply denounced the first session of a China- appointed legislature that will set Hong Kong's laws after the British colony reverts to Beijing's control this year.
"This was a bad day for Hong Kong," Patten said in a statement to the media after the Provisional Legislative Council met in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen to elect its president.
"The organisation that met over the border in Shenzhen has no legitimacy, no credibility and no authority in Hong Kong. I hope it will not embarrass Hong kong too much," he said.

Patten's comments were the latest salvo in a war of words between Chinese and British authorities over Patten's introduction of democratic reforms after taking office in 1992 and China's plans to scrap those changes after taking back Hong Kong at midnight on June 30.
At the Shenzhen meeting, the 60-member provisional legislature elected veteran pro-Beijing politician Rita Fan as its president, a position akin to parliamentary speaker.
Britain has refused to recognise the body, saying it has no legal basis in the handover treaty or in the future constitution of Hong Kong that was agreed between London and Beijing.
Beijing plans to install the legislature on July 1 to replace the present elected Legislative Council.

The dispute was fuelled further last week when a China- controlled panel overseeing the transfer of sovereignty announced plans to scrap a slew of Hong Kong laws including legislation that protects human rights and basic political freedoms in the territory of 6.3 million people.
